Unofficial integration, not affiliated with Energinet nor with Eloverblik. It
reads the hourly electricity consumption of your Danish metering points through
the **official customer API of Eloverblik** (Energinet DataHub) and feeds the
energy monitoring of Gladys with it. Read-only: nothing is ever changed on your
account.

> This integration has never been tested with a real Eloverblik account: it is
> written from the official API description (Swagger). Feedback is welcome.

## What you need

- A Danish electricity metering point (consumption) and MitID to log in to
  [eloverblik.dk](https://eloverblik.dk/).
- Gladys 5.3.0 or later.

## Create the token

1. Log in to [eloverblik.dk](https://eloverblik.dk/) with MitID (private
   customer).
2. Make sure your metering points are linked to your account (they appear on
   the home page).
3. Open the **Data sharing** menu (_Datadeling_), then create a token for the
   API. Give it a name, for example "Gladys", and copy it: it is a long text in
   three parts separated by dots, shown only once.
4. In Gladys, open the integration, paste the token in **Eloverblik token**
   and save.

The token is valid for **one year**. The status of the integration shows the
date it ends: create a new one on eloverblik.dk before that date and save it
in Gladys.

The token is kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, and sent only
to Eloverblik (`api.eloverblik.dk`). It is never written in the logs, the
status nor `/data`.

## Create the devices

After saving, the integration lists your **consumption** metering points (type
E17; production points are not read, 10 points at most). Open **Discovery**
and create the devices you want: each one is named "Eloverblik meter …1234"
(the last 4 digits of the metering point id only) and has a single feature,
**Consumption (30 min)**.

Only the created devices are read. The **Test the token** button asks for an
access token and lists your points (at most once a minute).

## How the data arrives

- Eloverblik publishes the consumption **one or two days late**. The
  integration reads once a day, from 09:00 (Danish time, a minute proper to
  your installation, up to 12:00), and asks only for the days not yet
  complete. While yesterday is incomplete, it reads again 4 hours later, 4
  scheduled reads a day at most. A device created, a new token or a Test that
  succeeds brings a read a minute later on top of them; the reads always stay
  an hour apart otherwise, and within 30 requests a day.
- At the first read, it takes **31 days** back, never before the day the
  metering point became yours (`consumerStartDate` of Eloverblik). If DataHub
  answers that the period starts before its registration (30018) or before
  the authorization (30010), that point's first accepted day is searched alone,
  by halves down to the day (no day lost), 8 requests at most per read for all
  the points (one more, once per run, if DataHub refuses quarter hours during
  a search); a search cut there publishes nothing yet (status `start_search`) and goes on at the next read. Each distinct start
  is asked in its own request, so a recent point never makes the others fail. After a stop, it catches up at
  most 92 days back. The last 3 complete days are read again with the next
  days: an estimated value replaced by a measured one is corrected.
- The integration asks for **quarter hours** and adds them two by two (the
  energy monitoring of Gladys works by half hours); when DataHub refuses that
  aggregation (30008, 30011), it asks for hours and splits each one in **two
  equal half hours** (until a restart). A half hour with a missing quarter
  stays unknown. An hour Eloverblik marks as not available
  (quality A02) or incomplete (A05) stays **unknown**: it is never counted as 0. A day with a missing hour is asked again for 10 days, then given up.
- The consumption goes into the energy monitoring with the date of each half
  hour (`publishEnergyConsumption`): there is no cumulative index, and no live
  value.

## Costs and energy contracts

This integration has no contract of its own. To see costs, attach an energy
contract to the consumption in Gladys, for example the Danish contract of the
**Energi Data Service** integration (grid tariffs, Energinet, elafgift and
DK1/DK2 spot prices). Danish tariffs that depend on the hour need the
30-minute consumption: this is what this integration publishes.

## Limits of the Eloverblik API

The integration stays far below the published limits: at most 30 requests a
day, one at a time, 2 seconds apart; the data access token (valid 24 hours) is
kept in memory and renewed after 20 hours; two token requests are never closer
than 5 minutes, even after a restart (the time is kept in `/data`; the limit
is 2 a minute per IP).

- **429 (too many requests)** or **503 (DataHub unavailable)** and other 5xx:
  every request pauses: 15 minutes, doubled each time up to 6 hours, or the
  `Retry-After` of the answer when it is longer (6 hours at most). The pause survives a restart.
- **Refused token** (the token request answers a 401 or 403 with an empty
  body, a JSON body or a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` header, or one of the
  error codes 50000 / 50001; a non-empty HTML page of a proxy is not a
  refusal): nothing is asked any more; the status says so. Save a new token,
  or press Test once the token works again.
- A 401 or 403 on a **data** route is not a refusal of your token: the access
  token is dropped and a new one is asked at the next read.
- An error on one metering point (no data, relation expired, ...) is shown in
  the status with its code (for example `E30015`); that point is asked again
  the next day only, the other points go on.

## What `/data` keeps

`/data/eloverblik.json` keeps: the time of the last read and of the last token
request, the count of requests of the day, the pause, a mark of a refused
token (8 bits of a salted hash, nothing to find the token back from) and, per
metering point (named by a keyed hash, never its id), the last complete day.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Eloverblik lists no consumption metering point"**: link your metering
  points on eloverblik.dk (the token only sees the points linked to your
  account).
- **"Meter …1234: E20010"** (relation not found) or **E30016** (relation
  expired): link the metering point again on eloverblik.dk.
- **"E30015"**: no data for the period yet; it is asked again the next day.
- **"not_listed"**: a created device is no longer among the metering points
  of the token.
- The Gladys time zone should be the Danish one (or the same clock): the days
  are Danish days.

## Data source

Data: Eloverblik, Energinet DataHub, your own meter data, read with the token
you created.

## Konfigurationseinstellungen

Diese Einstellungen fragt Eloverblik (Denmark) in seinem Konfigurationsbildschirm in Gladys ab.

| Einstellung | Typ | Pflichtfeld | Beschreibung |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Eloverblik token | `section` | Nein | Unofficial connector, not affiliated with Energinet. On eloverblik.dk, log in with MitID, link your metering points, then create a token (Data sharing / API). The integration reads, once a day, the consumption of every metering point you create in Discovery; Eloverblik serves it one or two days late, so the energy monitoring of Gladys fills up after the fact (quarter hours added two by two, or each hour in two half hours). Read-only. The token is valid for a year: create a new one before it ends (the status shows the date). For the costs, pair it with an energy contract (for example the Energi Data Service integration for Danish tariffs and spot prices). |
| Eloverblik token | `secret` | Ja | The token created on eloverblik.dk (a long text in three parts separated by dots). Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only to Eloverblik (api.eloverblik.dk). |

## So installierst du Eloverblik (Denmark) in Gladys

1. Öffne in Gladys **Integrationen**: Eloverblik (Denmark) erscheint im Katalog neben den nativen Integrationen, mit einem Community-Badge.
2. Klicke auf **Installieren**. Gladys lädt das Docker-Image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-eloverblik:0.1.1`) herunter, startet es in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox und erzeugt die Oberfläche der Integration (Geräte, Erkennung und Konfiguration).
3. Öffne den Bildschirm **Konfiguration** der Integration, fülle die Einstellungen aus und speichere.
4. Du kannst sie auch direkt über die URL ihres Repositorys installieren: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-eloverblik](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-eloverblik).

Eloverblik (Denmark) benötigt Gladys `>=5.3.0`. Der Katalog in Gladys wird stündlich aktualisiert, eine neue Version ist also spätestens eine Stunde nach ihrer Veröffentlichung verfügbar.

Du nutzt Gladys noch nicht? Es ist kostenlos und Open Source: [folge der Installationsanleitung](/de/docs/), um loszulegen.

## Über externe Integrationen

Eloverblik (Denmark) ist eine **externe Integration**: eine Community-Integration, die als Docker-Container verpackt und auf GitHub veröffentlicht wird. Gladys installiert sie mit einem Klick und führt sie in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox aus.
